analysis.title: "Markets May Not Wait": BofA Says AI Equity Vol Hasn't Caught Up With What Credit Already Knows
key_insights: BofA's equity derivatives team (Benjamin Bowler et al.) finds hyperscaler bond spreads and CDS at the widest levels in at least five years, while their forward P/E multiples and implied vols have barely moved.
Credit strategists project that if this year's issuance pace continues, five hyperscalers go from 3% of the US IG corporate bond index at end-2025 to 6.3% by end-2027.
Hyperscaler bond issuance rose from $17B in 2024 to $182B this year, per Hartnett as cited in the article.

Hyperscaler spreads are about 140bps (read off a chart, approximate), the widest in the five years BofA tracks. Spreads sit about 2.5 standard deviations above their five-year average, while 1-year 20-delta put vols are only about 1 standard deviation rich.

BofA says the disconnect can persist or widen without a catalyst. Equity vol would likely catch up quickly if higher leverage exposes untested vulnerabilities or if fundraising pressure challenges revenue expectations. Markets may not wait for AI earnings to disappoint, since a reflexive deterioration in sentiment from funding concerns could by itself lift equity vol.
BofA attributes the lack of equity vol reaction to positioning: the unwind of excess leverage built over the summer has suppressed volatility relative to what the credit signal implies.

Screen 1 (levels): the widest gaps between equity vol z-scores and spread z-scores are the hyperscalers (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, ORCL) and Nvidia, reflecting greater funding needs versus the net cash positions of other AI beneficiaries. Nvidia's spread z-score is well above 1 while its put vol z-score is negative.

Screen 2 (3-month changes): the biggest laggards are memory names. SK Hynix's vol is roughly 25 points below what its spreads imply, followed by Marvell and Micron. The article says chipmaker credit risk is trading wider than hyperscaler credit risk for the first time.

Trade: buy a Dec27 85-65% put spread on an equally weighted eight-name basket (Dassault Systemes, Amazon, Meta, Nokia, SAP, SK Hynix, ASML, Alphabet) for 3.11% premium, about 6.5x max payout, implied correlation about 27% on average. The long put is struck near mid-April levels, so it pays if the basket gives back most of its post-April gains.

The basket structure is long correlation as well as long vol. Average pairwise realized correlation among the eight names is around the 1st percentile of the past 10 years. BofA argues owning correlation hedges idiosyncratic concerns turning into a system-wide repricing across AI-exposed names.

BofA's CIO Michael Hartnett recently turned to buying hyperscaler/US tech bonds ("diamonds in the rough", tech bond returns relative to IG at 30-year lows), after a call a year ago to short hyperscaler bonds. The vol team instead bets equities are too complacent. Both agree credit has priced more AI pain than equities.

The vol team calls last Thursday's selloff (Nasdaq -6.4%, a -4.4 sigma move and worst day since Covid; S&P -4.4%, a -5.6 sigma event; VIX up nearly 11.6 points) a positioning-driven fragility event rather than a fully fundamental one, and sees material upside risk to US tech from these drawdown levels. Record inflows into SOXL, the 3x levered semis ETF, came on the day semis crashed.

Article context since BofA's data (through last Friday): Nomura's McElligott called Monday's ramp an "absolutely epic vol crush". On Tuesday a hot CPI print and Fed hawks pushed the 10Y back above 5% after a poorly received auction, and HY tech was the worst-performing credit sector. Fed Governor Bowman warned of a risk of a large correction in equity valuations tied to AI returns.

Recent funding events cited: Meta to sell up to $95B of stock instead of a jumbo bond, Microsoft seeking at least $25B in bonds, an off-balance-sheet AI obligations pile of $4.1T, and CoreWeave guiding to a $1.1B quarterly interest bill with $47B of debt. Nvidia is said to have lost about $1.2T in market cap in 10 days, and its CEO faces an independent board probe.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity vol and P/E multiples on AI beneficiaries are not pricing stress, and BofA sees material upside risk to US tech from drawdown levels. Last Thursday's selloff was positioning-driven rather than fundamental, and Hartnett now buys hyperscaler bonds as too gloomy.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler spreads sit about 2.5 standard deviations above their five-year average while put vols are only about 1 standard deviation rich. Equity vol could catch up rapidly on funding pressure, even without an earnings miss.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Per BofA the disconnect can persist or widen with no catalyst. The vol-catch-up view is invalidated if credit spreads narrow back toward equity-implied levels, or if funding concerns fail to challenge revenue expectations.

theme_stances.key_argument: Equity implied vol on AI beneficiaries lags the deterioration in credit and should catch up, potentially quickly on funding stress.
theme_stances.evidence: markets may not wait for the AI earnings impact to materialise

theme_stances.key_argument: Hyperscalers' share of the US IG index could double by end-2027 if the issuance pace continues, and credit markets may not absorb that much AI risk.
theme_stances.evidence: how much additional AI-related risk credit markets are willing to absorb
